[[File:酉の市Torinoichi000.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Tori-no-Ichi|lt=Tori-no-Ichi|lt=Torinoichi|de|Tori-no-Ichi|lt=Tori-no-Ichi|lt=Torinoichi|ja|酉の市|zh|酉の市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torinoichi|qq=}}の{{ill|Rake (tool)|en|Rake (tool)|qid=Q200822|lt=Kumade|1=Rake (tool)}}]]
'''Washi-no-Miya Shrine''' (鷲宮神社) is the name of a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine|1=Shinto shrine}}.

It is a branch of the Ōtori faith based on {{ill|Ōtori taisha|en|Ōtori taisha|qid=Q705151|lt=Ōtori Taisha|1=Ōtori taisha}}, though in many cases a Washi-no-Miya Shrine serves as the head shrine of the Kantō region’s {{ill|O-Tori-sama|de|O-Tori-sama|ja|お酉様|zh|O-Tori-sama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-Tori-sama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 酉の市|1=Tori-no-Ichi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11643942}} cult – notably the one enshrined in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}}’s {{ill|Kuki, Saitama|en|Kuki, Saitama|qid=Q47535|lt=Kuki City|1=Kuki, Saitama}}. The Washi-no-Miya Shrine in Kuki City was the head shrine (総社) of the {{ill|Ōta clan|en|Ōta clan|qid=Q1391922|lt=Fujiwara no Hidesato's|1=Ōta clan}} {{ill|Ota Villa|de|Ota-Anwesen|ja|太田荘|zh|太田荘|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Villa|1=Q11444411|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11444411}}, and many branch shrines exist mainly along the {{ill|Naka River (Saitama Tokyo)|en|Naka River (Saitama Tokyo)|qid=Q2613967|lt=Nakagawa|1=Naka River (Saitama Tokyo)}} region. In other areas, however, Washi-no-Miya Shrines are merely branches of other Ōtori faith shrines and may have no connection to the Kuki City shrine.

In addition, along the western part of the {{ill|Arakawa River (Kantō)|en|Arakawa River (Kantō)|qid=Q625465|lt=Arakawa|1=Arakawa River (Kantō)}} basin there is the {{ill|Hikawa Shrine|en|Hikawa Shrine|qid=Q5760456|lt=Hikawa Shrine|1=Hikawa Shrine}}, along the {{ill|Moto-Arakawa|de|Moto-Arakawa|ja|元荒川|zh|元荒川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Arakawa|1=Moto-Arakawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11388047}} basin there is the {{ill|Kuizu Shrine|de|Kuizu-Schrein|ja|久伊豆神社 (曖昧さ回避)|zh|久伊豆神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuizu Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 久伊豆神社|1=Hisaizu-jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55523154}}, and in the eastern and northern parts along the {{ill|Tone River|en|Tone River|qid=Q177452|lt=Tone River|1=Tone River}} and {{ill|Edo River|en|Edo River|qid=Q1194505|lt=Edogawa River|1=Edo River}} basins, many {{ill|Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Shrine|de|Katori-Schrein|ja|香取神社 (曖昧さ回避)|zh|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 香取神社}} are found. Occasionally, merged shrines such as {{ill|Washi Katori Shrine|de|Washi-Katori-Schrein|ja|鷲香取神社|zh|鷲香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washi Katori Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} or {{ill|Katori Washi Shrine|de|Katori-Washi-Schrein|ja|香取鷲神社|zh|香取鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Washi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} appear. Furthermore, since the term “宮” means “shrine,” many places today label their shrines as {{ill|Washi Shrine|de|Washi-Schrein|ja|鷲神社|zh|鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washi Shrine|1=Washi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11676283}} or {{ill|Nichiwashi Shrine|de|Nichiwashi-Schrein|ja|日鷲神社|zh|日鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nichiwashi Shrine|1=Ame-no-Hiwashi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65270357}}, even when their old or common names remain Washi-no-Miya. For example, there is the {{ill|Washi Shrine (Taitō)|de|Washi-Schrein (Taitō)|ja|鷲神社 (台東区)|zh|鷲神社 (台東区)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washi Shrine (Taitō)|1=Ōtori Shrine (Taito Ward)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11676284}}, in Taitō Ward, Tokyo (as inscribed on its torii plaque), the {{ill|Washi Shrine (Tsuchiura City, Higashizakicho)|de|Washi-Schrein (Tsuchiura City, Higashizakicho)|ja|鷲神社 (土浦市東崎町)|zh|鷲神社 (土浦市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washi Shrine (Tsuchiura City, Higashizakicho)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, in Tsuchiura City, Ibaraki, and the {{ill|Nichiwashi Shrine (Minamisoma City)|de|Nichiwashi-Schrein (Minamisoma City)|ja|日鷲神社 (南相馬市)|zh|日鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nichiwashi Shrine (Minamisoma City)|1=Hiwashi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11510871}}, in Minamisoma City, Fukushima.

As a {{ill|religious corporation|de|Religiöse Körperschaft|ja|宗教法人|zh|宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/religious corporation|qq=}}, there are nationwide 22 Washi-no-Miya Shrines and 2 Washi-no-Miya Associations.

See also {{ill|Ōtori Shrine|de|Ōtori-Schrein|ja|大鳥神社 (曖昧さ回避)|zh|大鳥神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtori Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Washi Shrine|de|Washi-Schrein|ja|鷲神社|zh|鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washi Shrine|1=Washi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11676283}}, {{ill|Great Washi Shrine|de|Großer Washi-Schrein|ja|大鷲神社|zh|大鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Washi Shrine|1=Ōwashi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65258950}}, and {{ill|Nichiwashi Shrine|de|Nichiwashi-Schrein|ja|日鷲神社|zh|日鷲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nichiwashi Shrine|1=Ame-no-Hiwashi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65270357}}.
